vocabulary.meaning: to believe that someone is honest
to disagree or fight with words
a person you know, but not well
ideas or suggestions about what someone should do
always supporting your friend or partner

grammar_tips.title: Present Simple for Relationships
grammar_tips.explanation: Use the present simple to talk about your relationships: 'I trust my best friend.'

grammar_tips.title: Talking About Experiences
grammar_tips.explanation: Use the present perfect for life experiences: 'We have known each other for five years.'

grammar_tips.title: Using 'get along' and 'get on'
grammar_tips.explanation: 'Get along' or 'get on' means to have a good relationship: 'I get along with my classmates.'

example_sentences.sentence: She is my close friend. We share everything.
It is important to trust and support each other.
Sometimes friends argue, but they make up quickly.
He gave me good advice when I had a problem.
I get along well with my cousins.

vocabulary.question: An _____ is a person you know but not very well.
Which word means 'to have a good relationship'?

sentence.question: We have _____ (known/argued) each other for many years.
Arrange: good / get / classmates / I / along / my / with
options: I get along with my classmates.

sentence.question: It is important to _____ (share/argue) your feelings.
Arrange: gives / advice / she / good / me

listening.question: Listen: Who does Tom get along with?
Listen: How long have Maria and Anna known each other?
Listen: Why did John argue with his friend?
Listen: What advice did Sarah give?
Listen: What does Emily share with her friends?

speaking.question: Describe your best friend.
speaking.answer: My best friend is funny, loyal, and always supports me.

speaking.question: Talk about a time you helped a friend.
speaking.answer: I helped my friend with homework when he did not understand it.

speaking.question: Explain how you give advice to your friends.
speaking.answer: I listen to my friends and then give advice if they need help.

speaking.question: Describe a time you argued with someone and made up.
speaking.answer: Last week, I argued with my friend about a game, but we made up quickly.

speaking.question: Say why trust is important in a relationship.
speaking.answer: Trust is important because it helps people feel safe and happy together.
